primary_classification.classification_basis: Inferential Evidence–Authority Conflation is supported in this occurrence because In this occurrence, an uncertain facial-recognition match was reportedly allowed to contribute to coercive public action without adequate independent identity corroboration and timely contestability.

assessment_boundaries: The record does not determine civil liability or the final merits of Reid's lawsuit.
The classification does not assert that every facial-recognition match is unreliable or unusable; it concerns the level of authority afforded to an uncertain match in this occurrence.
Population-level demographic accuracy concerns are context and are not used to manufacture an occurrence-specific discrimination finding.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Associated Press reports that Randall Reid was arrested in Georgia on a Louisiana warrant after facial-recognition technology linked him to a theft, despite Reid saying he had never been to Louisiana; he spent six days in jail before the warrant was withdrawn. The reporting describes the detective as relying on the facial-recognition result without further corroborating investigation and records continuing psychological and professional consequences. AIID is retained as a registry cross-reference rather than the principal evidentiary basis.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The governance issue is the promotion of a probabilistic identity lead into coercive authority. Facial recognition can generate an investigative candidate, but that candidate should remain an inference until independently corroborated against readily material facts such as location, physical characteristics and other evidence. A human warrant workflow does not cure automation bias if the human process merely carries the algorithmic candidate forward without genuinely independent identity assurance.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000005 shows why consequential public-authority systems need a hard separation between machine-generated identity leads and identity determinations. Verification must be independent enough to falsify the machine lead, and contestability must become effective before or promptly after liberty-affecting action.
